evidence: app/src/document.ts:1 — templates render via @gracile/gracile/server-html, a re-export of Lit's @lit-labs/ssr (officially 'experimental' per lit.dev/docs/ssr/overview)
app/src/lib/components.ts:1 — same labs-backed html export used for every shared component

app/package.json:11 — framework itself is pre-1.0 and self-described 'alpha state' (gracile.js.org/docs/), used in every route file (app/src/routes/(home).ts:1, app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].ts:1, etc.)
app/package.json:17 — Vite 8 (Rolldown) stable only since 2026-03-12, ~7 months before today
app/src/client/interactions.ts:1-115 — client layer is plain DOM JS, no experimental hydration/island APIs
app/vite.config.js:5 — only framework flag is the documented output: 'server' mode
reach.rationale: No experimental flags or directly-imported labs packages, but every page's rendering rests on Lit Labs SSR (experimental per lit.dev) inside a pre-1.0 alpha-labeled framework, plus a recently-stable Vite 8 — squarely 'recently-stable/experimental in central places'.

evidence: app/src/document.ts:1 and app/src/lib/components.ts:1 — the labs-backed html export is reached through exactly one framework module, uniformly
app/server.mjs:9-13 — the Hono adapter integration (gracile.honoAdapter, getClientBuildPath) is isolated in a single 19-line file
app/src/client/interactions.ts:1-115 — all interactivity is vanilla DOM code, avoiding @gracile/client/hydration surfaces entirely
app/src/ambient.d.ts:1 — framework ambient types pulled in via the official @gracile/gracile/ambient reference
containment.rationale: The experimental piece (labs SSR) is only reachable through the framework's documented server-html export, the server adapter lives in one file, and the client layer is framework-free; the only thing spread across files is the framework itself, which is inherent, not an experimental leak.

evidence: app/src/routes/(home).ts:1-2 — Gracile is spec-mandated; server-html is its only documented template mechanism, so the labs-SSR dependency is unavoidable
app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].ts:19 — responseInit.status = 404 uses the documented engine Handler context field to satisfy the spec's 404 encouragement rather than an experimental status API
app/src/client/interactions.ts:50-70 — filters use plain URL navigation instead of newer client-side routing/hydration layers, the least experimental option available
app/package.json:11-17 — every dependency is either the mandated framework or boringly stable (hono 4.x, @hono/node-server 2.x, Vite 8 within the engine's ^7||^8 peer range)
justification.rationale: Each non-long-stable dependency is either forced by the spec (Gracile, and therefore labs SSR) or the framework's own supported current release (Vite 8), and where the app had a choice it consistently picked the less experimental option.

findings.issue: All HTML rendering depends on @lit-labs/ssr, which Lit's current docs still classify as experimental/'pre-release software'; it is reached via @gracile/gracile/server-html but a breaking change upstream flows straight into every page.
findings.suggestion: Keep the lockfile pinned (it already is) and treat @gracile/gracile and @lit-labs/ssr upgrades as one unit; note in the README that the server-html import site is the single place to update if Gracile's SSR story changes.

findings.issue: The entire app rests on @gracile/gracile 0.11.0, a pre-1.0 release whose own docs say the project is in an 'alpha state'; 0.x semver allows breaking changes in minor releases (npm already shows 0.7.6-next pre-releases of @gracile/server).
findings.suggestion: Pin the exact version, upgrade deliberately on Gracile releases, and keep route files thin (they already are) so framework churn is cheap to absorb.

findings.issue: Vite 8 (Rolldown-based) is the most recent stable major (2026-03-12), a large bundler architecture change; slightly newer than the ~6-month 'recently-stable' window.
findings.suggestion: Fine as-is since @gracile/engine peer-supports ^7||^8; watch Vite 8.x minors for Rolldown plugin-compatibility notes when bumping.

findings.issue: responseInit.status relies on an engine API documented in the Handler typings ('Let you mutate the downstream page response') but not on the Gracile docs website itself — a slightly under-documented surface used in four route files.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable; if it disappears, the 404-not-found pattern can fall back to returning a Response directly, which the same handler API documents.

summary: The app's own code contains zero experimental flags, preview APIs or direct labs imports; its only genuinely experimental-staged dependency, Lit Labs SSR, is inherited through the spec-mandated Gracile framework's documented server-html export and is used uniformly and idiomatically. The residual risk is that everything sits on a pre-1.0, self-described-alpha framework plus the recently-stable Vite 8, which the app mitigates with a conservative vanilla-JS client layer and a single-file Hono adapter. Overall exposure is modest and unavoidable given the framework requirement.
